instantiated_cells.justification: The statute defines lobbying as "attempting to influence legislative or administrative action by oral or written communication," enumerating only oral and written communication types.

A lobbyist is any individual employed by or contracting with a principal whose duties include lobbying; principals include associations, corporations, LLCs, and partnerships, covering professional lobbyists and in-house lobbyists for companies and organizations, but state agencies are excluded as principals (per AG opinion) and government employees are exempt under §13.621(3).
The definitions section does not include a definition of "public entity"; it defines "agency," "business entity," "principal," etc., but not "public entity."

The statute provides a materiality threshold: principals anticipating ≤$500 in lobbying expenditures per calendar year may file a verified statement exempting them from licensing/registration/reporting, and registration is only required when expenditures exceed $500.

Lobbying covers communications with "any elective state official, agency official or legislative employee," and "legislative action" expressly includes action of the governor in approving/vetoing bills, capturing both legislative and executive (including governor) officials.

Lobbying targets include elective state officials (legislative branch), agency officials (executive/administrative bureaucracy), and legislative employees (staff), covering legislators, executive officials, senior agency officials, and staff.

Lobbying definition covers communications with elective state officials, agency officials, and legislative employees, and legislative action explicitly includes the governor's actions, so executive and legislative officials including the governor are covered.

Same as above: the definition of lobbying covers communications with state elective officials, agency officials, and legislative employees, with legislative action including the governor's bill approval/veto.
Lobbying expressly includes communications with elective state officials, agency officials, and legislative employees, and legislative action includes the governor's action on bills.

Lobbying targets cover elective state officials, agency officials (administrative branch/senior officials), and legislative employees (staff/members of legislature), spanning legislative and executive branches.

Elective state officials, local officials, tribal officials, and legislative employees acting in an official capacity are expressly exempted from the licensing/registration/reporting requirements (§§13.63, 13.64, 13.65, 13.68, 13.695), so elected officials are not required to register for lobbying-related behaviors.

The lobbyist definition contains a time standard (5 days within a reporting period of lobbying communications) and compensation standard (receipt of economic consideration other than expense reimbursement), and §13.695 separately requires agencies to report public employees engaged in legislative activity with proportionate time disclosure.
The definitions in §13.62 do not rely on any concept of public charter or special government protection in defining lobbyist, principal, or related terms.
The definitions in §13.62 do not rely on ownership as a definitional criterion for lobbyist, principal, or other regulated actors.
The statutory definitions do not depend on structure or composition of revenue; "business entity" is defined as any for-profit organization without reference to revenue composition.
